finding: The interactive startup screen allowed Pair before protected enrollment restore finished. Pair checked only in-memory enrollment; a retained identity could be replaced, and a late restore could overwrite accepted local state.
change: Pairing joins a same-authority-epoch enrollment initialization before any native pairing request, then rechecks identity, epoch and busy state.
Successful initialization is cached for that authority epoch before publishing state. Enrollment and pending-conversation checkpoint become visible together; partial restoration cannot admit a chat.
Concurrent startup/pair operations share one restoration future. Cleanup checks epoch and exact future identity; an old load cannot clear a newer flight.
Forget advances the existing authority epoch, forcing a fresh load before a new pairing. Old completions cannot publish state or authorize a new pair.
A failed protected-store read blocks pairing without displaying backend payload; a later explicit attempt can retry. Existing native/store/delivery owners are unchanged.
newFlutterCases: JM05 completed enrollment initialization cannot reopen a stale load before pairing
JM05 enrollment and pending conversation publish together after restoration
JM05 pairing waits for retained enrollment and never replaces it during startup
JM05 concurrent startup and pairing share one load and one native operation
JM05 failed enrollment read blocks pairing and a later explicit attempt can retry
JM05 forgotten startup load cannot authorize pairing or clear a newer restoration
verification: Six controlled-future Flutter cases added; root text/diff review and GPT-6.1 Terra high prompt-only architecture/Flutter review. Reviewer-found second-load gap fixed using per-epoch initialization and atomic publication. No executable validation locally.
limits: Initialization is controller-owned and idempotent per authority epoch, not a watcher for unrelated external protected-store edits.
Epoch invalidation does not cancel an already issued native pairing effect or infer its remote outcome.
Fresh hosted Flutter analysis/tests and actual Android/iOS device, signing and release acceptance remain separate and open.
